docs.title: RPi Generator Control
docs.text: A production-ready, distributed generator control system for off-grid solar installations with Victron energy systems.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The RPi Generator Control system automates generator management for off-grid solar installations. When your Victron Cerbo GX determines that battery levels are low and generator power is needed, it sends a signal to GenMaster, which coordinates with GenSlave to physically start the generator.

  • Automated Control

    Automatic generator start/stop based on Victron signals, schedules, and manual commands.

    Generator Controls

  • Safety First

    Arming system, failsafe watchdog, and heartbeat monitoring ensure safe operation.

    GenSlave Setup

  • Scheduling

    Automated exercise runs and scheduled operations keep your generator healthy.

    Scheduling Guide

  • Notifications

    Get alerts via Telegram, Slack, email, and 80+ other services via Apprise.

    Notifications

docs.title: Automated Control
docs.text:
• Victron Integration - Monitors GPIO signal from Cerbo GX relay
  • Scheduled Runs - APScheduler-based scheduling with flexible timing
  • Exercise Runs - Regular maintenance runs to keep generator healthy
  • Manual Override - Force start/stop from web UI regardless of signals

docs.title: Reliability & Safety
docs.text:
• Arming System - Explicit arm/disarm prevents accidental operations
  • Heartbeat Monitoring - Continuous health checks between devices
  • Independent Failsafe - GenSlave auto-stops generator if communication lost
  • State Persistence - PostgreSQL database survives reboots

docs.title: Modern Interface
docs.text:
• Real-time Dashboard - Live status updates via WebSocket
  • Dark/Light Mode - System preference detection
  • Mobile Responsive - Works on any device
  • Container Management - Portainer integration

docs.title: Fuel Tracking
docs.text:
• Per-Run Tracking - Automatic fuel consumption calculation
  • Generator Profile - Store manufacturer, model, serial number
  • Usage History - Track runtime and fuel over time

docs.title: 1. Deploy GenMaster
docs.text:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/rjsears/pizero_generator_control.git
cd pizero_generator_control/genmaster

# Configure environment
cp .env.example .env
nano .env  # Edit settings

# Start services
docker compose up -d

docs.title: 2. Deploy GenSlave
docs.text:
# On Pi Zero 2W
mkdir -p /opt/genslave && cd /opt/genslave

# Download compose file
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/.../docker-compose.yaml

# Configure
echo "GENSLAVE_API_SECRET=your-secret" > .env

# Start
docker compose up -d

docs.title: 3. Configure Tailscale
docs.text:
# Install on both devices
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up

docs.title: 4. Access Web UI
docs.text: Open https://your-genmaster-ip and log in.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The RPi Generator Control system is a distributed two-device architecture for automated generator management. It uses a master-slave pattern where GenMaster (Raspberry Pi 5) handles the web interface, business logic, and Victron integration, while GenSlave (Pi Zero 2W) controls the physical relay for generator start/stop.

docs.title: Boot Sequence / Power Loss Recovery
docs.text:
Both GenMaster and GenSlave implement safety measures for power loss and reboot scenarios.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         POWER LOSS RECOVERY SEQUENCE                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                                     │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │                         GenSlave Boot Sequence                                │  │
│  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
│  │                                                                               │  │
│  │  1. systemd starts genslave.service                                           │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  2. relay.py imports automationhat                                            │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  3. RELAY SET TO OFF (line 37) ←── CRITICAL SAFETY: Hardware reset            │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  4. RelayService.__init__()                                                   │  │
│  │     - _armed = False ←── Always disarmed on boot                              │  │
│  │     - _mock_state = False                                                     │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  5. FailsafeMonitor starts                                                    │  │
│  │     - _last_heartbeat = None                                                  │  │
│  │     - Waits for heartbeats from GenMaster                                     │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  6. GenSlave READY (waiting for GenMaster heartbeat)                          │  │
│  │     - Armed state will sync from GenMaster via heartbeat                      │  │
│  │                                                                               │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                                     │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │                        GenMaster Boot Sequence                                │  │
│  ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  │
│  │                                                                               │  │
│  │  1. Docker starts containers (PostgreSQL, Redis, GenMaster, Nginx)            │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  2. StateMachine.initialize() loads from database                             │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► Log pre-boot state for debugging                                 │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► RESET automation_armed = False ←── ALWAYS disarm on boot         │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► RESET slave_connection_status = "unknown"                        │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► If generator_running was True:                                   │  │
│  │         │      - Set generator_running = False                                │  │
│  │         │      - Close orphaned run record (stop_reason = "power_loss")       │  │
│  │         │      - Log WARNING                                                  │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         └──► Log SYSTEM_BOOT_RESET event                                      │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  3. Services start (GPIO Monitor, Heartbeat, Scheduler)                       │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  4. Reconciliation with GenSlave                                              │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► Query GenSlave relay state: GET /api/relay/state                 │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► If slave unreachable:                                            │  │
│  │         │      - Log warning, continue (slave may boot later)                 │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ├──► If relay ON but generator_running = False:                       │  │
│  │         │      - Log RECONCILIATION_MISMATCH                                  │  │
│  │         │      - WARNING: Manual intervention may be required                 │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         └──► Update slave_connection_status = "connected"                     │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  5. Log SYSTEM_BOOT event                                                     │  │
│  │         │                                                                     │  │
│  │         ▼                                                                     │  │
│  │  6. GenMaster READY                                                           │  │
│  │     - Heartbeats start (sync armed state to GenSlave)                         │  │
│  │     - Victron signals IGNORED until armed                                     │  │
│  │     - Scheduled runs SKIPPED until armed                                      │  │
│  │                                                                               │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                              POST-BOOT STATE                                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                                     │
│  After any power loss or reboot:                                                    │
│                                                                                     │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  Component          │ State              │ Notes                            │    │
│  │  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│    │
│  │  GenMaster armed    │ False              │ ALWAYS reset on boot             │    │
│  │  GenSlave armed     │ False (synced)     │ Synced from GenMaster            │    │
│  │  GenSlave relay     │ OFF                │ Hardware safety reset            │    │
│  │  generator_running  │ False              │ Reset if was True                │    │
│  │  slave_connection   │ "unknown"→"connected" │ Updated by heartbeat          │    │
│  │  Victron response   │ DISABLED           │ Until operator arms              │    │
│  │  Scheduled runs     │ DISABLED           │ Until operator arms              │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                                     │
│  OPERATOR ACTION REQUIRED:                                                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  1. Verify GenSlave connection in web UI (should show "connected")          │    │
│  │  2. Review system status and any warning messages                           │    │
│  │  3. Click "Arm Automation" or POST /api/system/arm                          │    │
│  │  4. System now responds to Victron signals and schedules                    │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Reconciliation Events
docs.text: Event Severity Description SYSTEM_BOOT_RESET WARNING/INFO Logged on every boot with pre-boot state RECONCILIATION_MISMATCH WARNING GenSlave relay ON but no active run in GenMaster

docs.title: Database Fields Reset on Boot
docs.text:
-- Always reset
automation_armed = False
automation_armed_at = NULL
automation_armed_by = NULL
slave_connection_status = 'unknown'
missed_heartbeat_count = 0

-- Reset if generator was running
generator_running = False
run_trigger = 'idle'
generator_start_time = NULL
current_run_id = NULL  -- After closing orphaned run

docs.title: Arming Integration Points
docs.text:
1. Victron Signal Handler (handle_victron_signal_change)
  2. Checks automation_armed before taking action

  3. Logs signal changes regardless of arm state

  4. Start Generator (start_generator)

  5. can_start_generator() requires automation_armed == true

  6. Returns clear error: "Cannot start - automation is not armed"

  7. Scheduler (_execute_scheduled_run)

  8. Checks is_armed() before executing

  9. Logs skipped runs with reason

  10. Full Status (get_full_status)

  11. Includes automation_armed in system status response

docs.title: Development/Testing Mode (LXC Containers)
docs.text: GenMaster can run in LXC containers for testing without real GPIO hardware.

docs.title: Auto-Detection
docs.text:
• GenMaster automatically detects when NOT running on a Raspberry Pi
  • Falls back to mock GPIO mode (checks /proc/cpuinfo for "Raspberry Pi")
  • Development API becomes available at /api/dev/*
  • Set GENSLAVE_ENABLED=false in .env for UI-only testing (disables heartbeat)

docs.title: Development API Endpoints
docs.text:
When in mock mode, these endpoints simulate Victron GPIO signals:

GET  /api/dev/status           - Development mode status
GET  /api/dev/gpio/state       - Current mock GPIO state
POST /api/dev/gpio/victron-signal  - Simulate Victron signal {"active": true/false}
POST /api/dev/gpio/toggle      - Toggle signal state
POST /api/dev/gpio/reset       - Reset to inactive
POST /api/dev/webhook/test     - Test webhook delivery

docs.title: Testing a Generator Cycle
docs.text:
# Start GenMaster (auto-detects LXC/dev environment)
docker compose up -d

# Simulate Victron requesting generator
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/dev/gpio/victron-signal \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"active": true}'

# Watch state transition: IDLE → STARTING → RUNNING

# Simulate Victron releasing generator
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/dev/gpio/victron-signal \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"active": false}'

# Watch state transition: RUNNING → STOPPING → IDLE

See LXC-TESTING.md for complete setup instructions.

docs.title: Cloudflare Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to configure Cloudflare Tunnel for secure remote access to GenMaster.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Overview
  • Prerequisites
  • Creating a Tunnel
  • Docker Configuration
  • DNS Configuration
  • Security Considerations
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Cloudflare Tunnel provides secure remote access to GenMaster without exposing ports on your router or requiring a static IP address.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text: Feature Description No port forwarding Tunnel connects outbound to Cloudflare Built-in SSL Automatic HTTPS with Cloudflare certificates DDoS protection Cloudflare's network protects your origin Zero Trust Optional Access policies for authentication No static IP Works with dynamic IP addresses

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Cloudflare account (free tier works)
  2. Domain name added to Cloudflare
  3. Docker running on GenMaster

docs.title: Step 1: Access Zero Trust Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Log in to dash.cloudflare.com
  2. Navigate to Zero Trust (or one.dash.cloudflare.com)
  3. Go to Networks > Tunnels

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Tunnel
docs.text:
1. Click Create a tunnel
  2. Select Cloudflared as the connector
  3. Name your tunnel (e.g., genmaster-tunnel)
  4. Click Save tunnel

docs.title: Step 3: Get Your Token
docs.text:
After creating the tunnel, you'll see a token. It looks like:

eyJhIjoiNzM0MzU5NmQ1ZmM4N2I2MjE5NmY5...

Copy this token - you'll need it for Docker configuration.

docs.title: Step 4: Configure Public Hostname
docs.text:
1. In the tunnel settings, click Public Hostname
  2. Add a hostname:
  3. Subdomain: generator (or your choice)
  4. Domain: Select your domain
  5. Service Type: HTTPS
  6. URL: nginx:443
  7. Under Additional settings:
  8. Enable No TLS Verify (for self-signed certs)
  9. Or use HTTP if preferred

docs.title: Environment Variable
docs.text:
Add to your .env file:

CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=eyJhIjoiNzM0MzU5NmQ1ZmM4N2I2MjE5NmY5...

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
The cloudflared service is defined with a profile:

cloudflared:
  image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
  container_name: genmaster_cloudflared
  command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run
  environment:
    - TUNNEL_TOKEN=${CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN}
  restart: unless-stopped
  networks:
    - genmaster-external
  profiles:
    - cloudflare

docs.title: Starting the Tunnel
docs.text:
# Start with Cloudflare profile enabled
docker compose --profile cloudflare up -d

# Check tunnel status
docker compose logs cloudflared

# Verify tunnel is connected
docker compose ps cloudflared

docs.title: Verifying Connection
docs.text:
1. Check Cloudflare Dashboard: Tunnel should show Healthy
  2. Visit your hostname: https://generator.yourdomain.com
  3. Check logs: docker compose logs -f cloudflared

docs.title: Automatic (Recommended)
docs.text: When you add a public hostname to your tunnel, Cloudflare automatically creates a CNAME record pointing to your tunnel.

docs.title: Manual Configuration
docs.text:
If you need to configure DNS manually:

  1. Go to DNS in Cloudflare Dashboard
  2. Add a CNAME record:
  3. Name: generator
  4. Target: <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com
  5. Proxy status: Proxied (orange cloud)

docs.title: Cloudflare Access (Optional)
docs.text:
For additional security, add authentication via Cloudflare Access:

  1. Go to Zero Trust > Access > Applications
  2. Click Add an application
  3. Select Self-hosted
  4. Configure:
  5. Application name: GenMaster
  6. Subdomain: generator
  7. Domain: Your domain
  8. Add an Access Policy:
  9. Rule action: Allow
  10. Include: Emails ending in @yourdomain.com
  11. Or use one-time PIN, Google auth, etc.

docs.title: IP Restrictions
docs.text:
The tunnel accepts all traffic from Cloudflare. For additional security:

  1. Configure Nginx to only accept Cloudflare IPs
  2. Or use Access policies as described above

docs.title: Firewall
docs.text:
Since the tunnel connects outbound, you don't need to open any ports. However, ensure:

  • Outbound HTTPS (443) is allowed
  • The cloudflared container can reach the internet

docs.title: Multiple Services
docs.text: You can route multiple services through one tunnel:

docs.title: GenMaster Web UI
docs.text:
Public hostname: generator.yourdomain.com
Service: https://nginx:443

docs.title: Portainer (Optional)
docs.text:
Public hostname: portainer.yourdomain.com
Service: http://portainer:9000

docs.title: API Only
docs.text:
Public hostname: api.yourdomain.com
Service: https://nginx:443
Path: /api/*

docs.title: Tunnel Not Connecting
docs.text:
1. Check token: 

    echo $CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN | head -c 20
    Verify it matches the dashboard.

  2. Check container logs: 

    docker compose logs cloudflared

  3. Check network access: 

    docker compose exec cloudflared ping -c 3 cloudflare.com

docs.title: 502 Bad Gateway
docs.text:
The tunnel is connecting but can't reach your service:

  1. Check nginx is running: 

    docker compose ps nginx

  2. Verify service URL:

  3. Should be nginx:443 or genmaster:8000

  4. Not localhost (containers are isolated)

  5. Check TLS settings:

  6. Enable "No TLS Verify" for self-signed certs
  7. Or configure proper certificates

docs.title: Tunnel Keeps Reconnecting
docs.text:
1. Check for conflicts:

  2. Only one cloudflared should run per tunnel

  3. Check resources: 

    docker stats cloudflared

  4. Update cloudflared: 

    docker compose pull cloudflared
docker compose --profile cloudflare up -d

docs.title: Access Denied (403)
docs.text:
If using Cloudflare Access:

  1. Check your email is in the allowed list
  2. Clear browser cookies
  3. Try incognito mode
  4. Check Access policy configuration

docs.title: Updating Cloudflared
docs.text:
docker compose pull cloudflared
docker compose --profile cloudflare up -d

docs.title: Rotating Tunnel Token
docs.text:
1. Go to Cloudflare Dashboard
  2. Delete the old tunnel
  3. Create a new tunnel
  4. Update CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN
  5. Restart cloudflared

docs.title: Disabling Tunnel
docs.text:
# Stop cloudflared only
docker compose --profile cloudflare stop cloudflared

# Or start without cloudflare profile
docker compose up -d  # Doesn't include cloudflare profile

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use Access policies for authentication
  2. Monitor tunnel health in Cloudflare Dashboard
  3. Set up alerts for tunnel disconnections
  4. Keep cloudflared updated for security patches
  5. Use separate tunnels for production and development

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Tailscale Setup - VPN alternative for local network
  • Notifications - Get alerts for system events
  • Troubleshooting - Common issues and solutions

docs.title: Diagnostic Checklist (Do This First)
docs.text: When asked to check/fix Cloudflare Tunnel real IP issues, follow these steps:

docs.title: Step 1: Confirm the Problem Exists
docs.text:
# Check nginx logs - look for Docker IPs (172.x.x.x) instead of real client IPs
docker logs <nginx_container> --tail 20

# If you see entries like:
# 172.18.0.1 - - [10/Feb/2026:16:00:00 +0000] "GET / HTTP/1.1" ...
# ^^^^^^^^^^^ This is a Docker IP - THE PROBLEM EXISTS

# If you see real external IPs (like 98.173.x.x), the fix is already in place

docs.title: Step 2: Check if real_ip Config Exists in nginx
docs.text:
# Check if nginx has the real_ip configuration
docker exec <nginx_container> grep -A5 "real_ip" /etc/nginx/nginx.conf

# If this returns nothing or no "set_real_ip_from" lines, THE FIX IS NEEDED

docs.title: Step 3: Find Where nginx.conf Comes From
docs.text:
# Check if nginx.conf is mounted from host
docker inspect <nginx_container> --format '{{json .Mounts}}' | jq .

# Look for a bind mount like:
# "Source": "/path/to/nginx.conf" -> this is where the file lives on host

# IMPORTANT: Check if there's a setup.sh or similar script that GENERATES nginx.conf
# If so, you must add the fix to the SCRIPT, not just the file
grep -r "nginx.conf" *.sh  # or similar to find generation scripts

docs.title: Step 4: Apply the Fix
docs.text: See "The Fix" section below. Remember: - If nginx.conf is a static file: edit the file directly - If nginx.conf is generated by a script: edit the SCRIPT's heredoc/template

docs.title: Step 5: Verify the Fix Works
docs.text:
# Reload nginx
docker exec <nginx_container> nginx -t && docker exec <nginx_container> nginx -s reload

# Make a request through Cloudflare and check logs
docker logs <nginx_container> --tail 5

# You should now see real client IPs, not 172.x.x.x

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
When using Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared) with nginx running in Docker, nginx sees all external traffic as coming from a Docker network IP (e.g., 172.18.0.1) instead of the real client IP.

Why this happens: 1. External client connects to Cloudflare 2. Cloudflare routes through the tunnel to the cloudflared container 3. cloudflared container forwards to nginx container 4. Both containers are on a Docker network 5. nginx sees the cloudflared container's Docker IP, not the real client

The consequence: - IP-based access control fails (all traffic appears "internal") - Rate limiting doesn't work properly (all traffic shares one IP) - Logs are useless for identifying clients

docs.title: Step 1: Add real_ip Configuration to nginx.conf
docs.text:
Add this block in the http section, BEFORE the geo block and log_format:

http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream;

    # ==========================================================================
    # Real IP Configuration for Cloudflare Tunnel
    # ==========================================================================
    # Trust Docker/internal networks as proxies (cloudflared connects from here)
    # This allows nginx to extract the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For header
    set_real_ip_from 172.16.0.0/12;
    set_real_ip_from 10.0.0.0/8;
    set_real_ip_from 192.168.0.0/16;
    set_real_ip_from 100.64.0.0/10;
    set_real_ip_from 127.0.0.1;

    # Cloudflare sets X-Forwarded-For with the real client IP
    real_ip_header X-Forwarded-For;

    # Enable recursive lookup (use rightmost untrusted IP in chain)
    real_ip_recursive on;

    # ... rest of config (log_format, geo block, etc.)

docs.title: Step 2: If nginx.conf is Generated by a Script
docs.text:
If your nginx.conf is generated by a setup script (like setup.sh), you must add the real_ip configuration to the script's heredoc/template, NOT just the file. Otherwise, your changes will be overwritten when the script runs again.

Look for something like: 

cat > nginx.conf << 'EOF'
http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream;
    # ADD THE real_ip CONFIG HERE

docs.title: Step 3: Reload nginx
docs.text:
# Test config first
docker exec <nginx_container> nginx -t

# If OK, reload
docker exec <nginx_container> nginx -s reload
# OR
docker restart <nginx_container>

docs.title: Test 1: Check nginx logs
docs.text:
Add $http_x_forwarded_for to your log format temporarily:

log_format main '$remote_addr - XFF:$http_x_forwarded_for - [$time_local] ...';

Reload nginx and make a request through Cloudflare: - XFF:- = Cloudflare is not sending the header (problem with Cloudflare config) - XFF:1.2.3.4 = Header is present, real_ip should extract it

docs.title: Test 2: Check $remote_addr
docs.text:
After the real_ip config is applied, $remote_addr in logs should show the real client IP, not 172.x.x.x.

Make a request from a known external IP and verify it shows in logs.

docs.title: Test 3: Verify access control works
docs.text:
1. Access through Cloudflare from an IP NOT in your allowed list
  2. You should get 403 Forbidden
  3. Check logs - you should see the real external IP with "external" access level

docs.title: What Each Directive Does
docs.text: Directive Purpose set_real_ip_from Trust these IPs as reverse proxies. When request comes from these IPs, look at headers for real IP. real_ip_header Which header contains the real client IP. Cloudflare uses X-Forwarded-For. real_ip_recursive on If there are multiple IPs in the header chain, find the rightmost one that's not trusted.

docs.title: Why X-Forwarded-For (not CF-Connecting-IP)
docs.text:
Cloudflare sets both headers: - CF-Connecting-IP: Cloudflare-specific header with client IP - X-Forwarded-For: Standard proxy header with client IP

Using X-Forwarded-For works for Cloudflare and is also compatible with other proxies (like Tailscale Serve if you use it).

docs.title: Issue: Still seeing Docker IPs after config change
docs.text:
• Cause: nginx wasn't reloaded
  • Fix: docker exec <container> nginx -s reload

docs.title: Issue: Config change doesn't persist
docs.text:
• Cause: nginx.conf is generated by a script that overwrites it
  • Fix: Add the config to the generation script, not just the file

docs.title: Issue: All traffic blocked after change
docs.text:
• Cause: real_ip is working but geo block doesn't include the real IPs
  • Fix: Add your allowed external IPs to the geo block

docs.title: Issue: XFF header is empty
docs.text:
• Cause: Cloudflare Tunnel not configured to forward headers
  • Fix: Check cloudflared/tunnel configuration in Cloudflare dashboard

docs.title: Quick Copy-Paste Block
docs.text:
# Real IP Configuration for Cloudflare Tunnel
    set_real_ip_from 172.16.0.0/12;
    set_real_ip_from 10.0.0.0/8;
    set_real_ip_from 192.168.0.0/16;
    set_real_ip_from 100.64.0.0/10;
    set_real_ip_from 127.0.0.1;
    real_ip_header X-Forwarded-For;
    real_ip_recursive on;

docs.title: Generator Control Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to start, stop, and monitor your generator using the RPi Generator Control system.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Overview
  • Understanding Generator States
  • Arming the System
  • Starting the Generator
  • Stopping the Generator
  • Override System
  • Runtime Limits
  • Fuel Tracking
  • Run History
  • API Reference

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The generator control system uses a master-slave architecture where GenMaster coordinates all operations and GenSlave physically controls the relay connected to your generator's two-wire start input.

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
1. GenMaster is the source of truth - The PostgreSQL database on GenMaster maintains the authoritative state of whether the generator should be running.

  2. Heartbeat synchronization - GenMaster sends heartbeats to GenSlave every 10 seconds. If GenSlave's relay state doesn't match GenMaster's intended state, the heartbeat corrects it.

  3. Safety first - The system defaults to a safe state:

  4. Relay is disarmed on boot (requires explicit arming)
  5. Generator can always be stopped even when disarmed
  6. GenSlave has an independent failsafe that stops the generator if communication is lost

docs.title: Understanding Generator States
docs.text: The state machine tracks the generator through several states:

docs.title: Generator Running States
docs.text: State Description idle Generator is off, system is waiting running Generator is actively running

docs.title: Trigger Types
docs.text:
When the generator starts, the system records what triggered it:

Trigger Description victron Started automatically by Victron Cerbo GX signal (low battery) manual Started manually via web UI or API scheduled Started by a scheduled run exercise Started by an exercise schedule for maintenance

docs.title: Stop Reasons
docs.text:
When the generator stops, the system records why:

Reason Description victron Victron signal went inactive (battery charged) manual Stopped manually via web UI or API scheduled_end Scheduled run duration completed exercise_end Exercise run completed comm_loss GenSlave lost communication with GenMaster override Force-stop override activated error An error occurred max_runtime Maximum runtime limit exceeded

docs.title: Arming the System
docs.text: The arming system is a safety feature that prevents accidental generator starts.

docs.title: Why Arming?
docs.text:
• Prevents unintended starts during maintenance
  • Requires explicit operator action to enable automation
  • Disarmed by default on system boot

docs.title: Arming Behavior
docs.text:
State Can Start (Auto) Can Start (Manual) Can Stop Disarmed No No Yes Armed Yes Yes Yes

Note: The generator can always be stopped for safety, regardless of arm state.

docs.title: How to Arm
docs.text:
Via Web UI: 1. Navigate to the Generator dashboard 2. Click the Arm button in the control panel 3. The status indicator will change to show "Armed"

Via API: 

# Arm the relay
curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/generator/arm \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

# Disarm the relay
curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/generator/disarm \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

docs.title: Auto-Arm on Connection Restore
docs.text:
If enabled via AUTO_ARM_RELAY_ON_CONNECT=true, the system will automatically arm the relay when GenSlave connection is restored after an outage. This feature respects manual disarms:

  • If you manually disarmed via the UI, auto-arm will not override your choice
  • If you manually arm via the UI, the "manual disarm" flag is cleared
  • Auto-arm only triggers when connection is restored, not on every heartbeat

docs.title: Automatic Start (Victron)
docs.text:
When Victron sends a "generator needed" signal (GPIO17 goes HIGH):

  1. System checks if relay is armed
  2. System checks for active override (force_stop blocks auto-start)
  3. System checks for runtime lockout or cooldown
  4. If all checks pass, generator starts

docs.title: Manual Start
docs.text:
Via Web UI: 1. Ensure the system is armed 2. Click Start Generator 3. Optionally set a duration for auto-stop 4. Confirm the action

Via API: 

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/generator/start \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"duration_minutes": 60, "notes": "Testing"}'

docs.title: What Happens on Start
docs.text:
1. Database updated first - GenMaster sets generator_running = true
  2. Relay command sent - GenMaster tells GenSlave to turn relay ON
  3. Run record created - Start time, trigger type, and fuel info logged
  4. Webhooks fired - generator.started.{trigger} event sent
  5. Notifications sent - If configured, push notification goes out

Even if the relay command fails (network issue), the next heartbeat will synchronize GenSlave with GenMaster's state.

docs.title: Automatic Stop (Victron)
docs.text: When the Victron signal goes LOW (battery charged): - System checks if the current run was triggered by Victron - If yes, generator stops automatically - If run was manual/scheduled, Victron signal is ignored

docs.title: Manual Stop
docs.text:
Via Web UI: Click Stop Generator - works even when disarmed.

Via API: 

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/generator/stop \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reason": "Maintenance needed"}'

docs.title: What Happens on Stop
docs.text:
1. Database updated first - GenMaster sets generator_running = false
  2. Relay command sent - GenMaster tells GenSlave to turn relay OFF
  3. Run record completed - Stop time, duration, fuel usage calculated
  4. Auto-stop jobs cancelled - Any scheduled auto-stop is removed
  5. Webhooks fired - generator.stopped.{reason} event sent
  6. Notifications sent - Runtime and fuel usage included in notification

docs.title: Override System
docs.text: Overrides let you force the generator into a specific state, ignoring normal triggers.

docs.title: Override Types
docs.text: Type Effect force_run Keeps generator running, ignores Victron "stop" signal force_stop Keeps generator stopped, blocks automatic Victron starts

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• force_stop only blocks automatic (Victron) starts
  • Manual and scheduled starts still work with force_stop active
  • Overrides persist until explicitly disabled

docs.title: Using Overrides
docs.text:
Via Web UI: 1. Navigate to Generator dashboard 2. Toggle the Override switch 3. Select override type (Force Run or Force Stop)

Via API: 

# Enable force_run override
curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/override/enable \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"override_type": "force_run"}'

# Disable override
curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/override/disable \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

docs.title: Runtime Limits
docs.text: Protect your generator from excessive runtime with configurable limits.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Setting Description Default runtime_limits_enabled Enable/disable the feature false max_run_minutes Maximum continuous runtime 480 (8 hours) cooldown_minutes Required rest after max runtime 60 lockout_on_max_runtime Require acknowledgment after max true

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. When generator reaches max_run_minutes, it automatically stops
  2. Stop reason is recorded as max_runtime
  3. If lockout_on_max_runtime is enabled:
  4. A lockout is activated
  5. Generator cannot restart until operator acknowledges the event
  6. If only cooldown is active:
  7. Generator waits cooldown_minutes before allowing restart
  8. Manual starts bypass cooldown

docs.title: Clearing Lockout
docs.text:
Via Web UI: 1. A banner appears indicating max runtime was reached 2. Click Acknowledge & Clear Lockout

Via API: 

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/generator/clear-lockout \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"acknowledge": true}'

docs.title: Fuel Tracking
docs.text: The system tracks estimated fuel consumption for each run.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set these in Settings > Generator Info:

Field Description Fuel Type lpg (Propane), natural_gas, or diesel Expected Load 50 or 100 percent Consumption @ 50% Gallons per hour at 50% load Consumption @ 100% Gallons per hour at 100% load

docs.title: How It's Calculated
docs.text:
estimated_fuel_used = (runtime_seconds / 3600) × fuel_consumption_rate

The consumption rate used is based on the expected load setting at the time the run started.

docs.title: Viewing Fuel Usage
docs.text:
Via Web UI: - Dashboard shows total fuel used since last reset - Each run in history shows individual fuel consumption

Via API: 

# Get fuel usage
curl https://your-genmaster/api/generator/fuel-usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

# Reset fuel tracking (e.g., after refueling)
curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/generator/fuel-usage/reset \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

docs.title: Run History
docs.text: Every generator run is logged with detailed information.

docs.title: What's Recorded
docs.text: Field Description start_time Unix timestamp when started stop_time Unix timestamp when stopped duration_seconds Total runtime trigger_type What started it (victron/manual/scheduled/exercise) stop_reason Why it stopped notes Optional user notes fuel_type_at_run Fuel type when run started load_at_run Load setting when run started estimated_fuel_used Calculated fuel consumption

docs.title: Viewing History
docs.text:
Via Web UI: Navigate to Generator > History to see all runs with filtering options.

Via API: 

# Get last 50 runs
curl "https://your-genmaster/api/generator/history?limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

# Filter by trigger type
curl "https://your-genmaster/api/generator/history?trigger_type=victron" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
Get aggregate statistics for a time period:

# Last 30 days (default)
curl "https://your-genmaster/api/generator/stats" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

# Last 90 days
curl "https://your-genmaster/api/generator/stats?days=90" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN"

Returns: - Total runs - Total runtime (hours) - Average runtime per run - Breakdown by trigger type

docs.title: Endpoints Summary
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/generator/state Get current generator status POST /api/generator/start Start the generator POST /api/generator/stop Stop the generator POST /api/generator/arm Arm the relay POST /api/generator/disarm Disarm the relay GET /api/generator/history Get run history GET /api/generator/stats Get runtime statistics GET /api/generator/fuel-usage Get fuel usage since reset POST /api/generator/fuel-usage/reset Reset fuel tracking GET /api/generator/runtime-limits Get runtime limits status POST /api/generator/clear-lockout Clear runtime lockout POST /api/override/enable Enable override POST /api/override/disable Disable override GET /api/override/status Get override status

docs.title: Response Examples
docs.text:
GET /api/generator/state 

{
  "running": true,
  "state": "running",
  "current_run_id": 42,
  "start_time": 1714567890,
  "runtime_seconds": 3600,
  "trigger": "victron",
  "armed": true,
  "slave_connected": true
}

GET /api/generator/stats 

{
  "period_days": 30,
  "total_runs": 15,
  "total_runtime_seconds": 54000,
  "total_runtime_hours": 15.0,
  "average_runtime_seconds": 3600,
  "runs_by_trigger": {
    "victron": 10,
    "manual": 3,
    "scheduled": 2
  },
  "runtime_by_trigger": {
    "victron": 36000,
    "manual": 10800,
    "scheduled": 7200
  }
}

docs.title: Safety Features Summary
docs.text: Feature Purpose Arming Prevents accidental starts, requires explicit operator action Heartbeat Sync Ensures GenSlave always matches GenMaster's intended state GenSlave Failsafe Independent watchdog stops generator if communication lost Runtime Limits Prevents generator damage from excessive continuous operation Lockout System Requires human acknowledgment after max runtime events Override Safety force_stop still allows manual intervention Relay OFF Always Works Can always stop generator regardless of arm state

docs.text:

  • Victron Integration - Configure GPIO signal monitoring
  • Notifications - Set up alerts for generator events
  • Troubleshooting - Common issues and solutions

docs.title: GenSlave Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to set up and configure GenSlave, the relay controller component that runs on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
• Overview
  • Hardware Requirements
  • Installation
  • Configuration
  • API Reference
  • Failsafe System
  • WiFi Configuration
  • Scheduled Reboot
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
GenSlave is a lightweight FastAPI application that:

  • Controls the relay connected to your generator's two-wire start input
  • Receives heartbeats from GenMaster and synchronizes state
  • Triggers failsafe if communication with GenMaster is lost
  • Displays status on the LCD screen (Automation Hat Mini)
  • Sends notifications via Apprise when failsafe triggers

docs.title: Raspberry Pi Zero 2W
docs.text: Spec Requirement Model Pi Zero 2W (recommended) or Pi Zero W RAM 512MB (sufficient for GenSlave) Storage 8GB+ microSD card Power 5V 2.5A power supply

docs.title: Automation Hat Mini
docs.text:
The Pimoroni Automation Hat Mini provides:

  • 1 Relay - 24V 2A switching (connects to generator)
  • 1 LCD - 160x80 pixel display for status
  • 3 Inputs - Digital/analog inputs (not used)
  • 1 Output - Additional output (not used)

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Connect the Automation Hat Mini relay to your generator's two-wire start terminal:

Automation Hat Mini          Generator
┌─────────────────┐          ┌─────────────────┐
│  RELAY NO  ─────┼──────────┤ START TERMINAL 1│
│  RELAY COM ─────┼──────────┤ START TERMINAL 2│
└─────────────────┘          └─────────────────┘
  • NO = Normally Open
  • COM = Common
  • Use appropriate gauge wire for your installation

Warning: Consult your generator's manual and a qualified electrician before making connections.

docs.title: Quick Start with Pre-built Image
docs.text:
# SSH into your Pi Zero 2W
ssh pi@your-pi-zero.local

# Create installation directory
sudo mkdir -p /opt/genslave
cd /opt/genslave

# Download docker-compose.yaml
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rjsears/pizero_generator_control/main/genslave/docker-compose.yaml

# Create .env file (see Configuration section)
nano .env

# Start GenSlave
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
If you need to build for your specific architecture:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/rjsears/pizero_generator_control.git
cd pizero_generator_control/genslave

# Build for ARM (Pi Zero)
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm/v7 -t genslave:local .

# Update docker-compose.yaml to use local image
# Change: image: rjsears/pizero_generator_control:genslave
# To: image: genslave:local

docker compose up -d

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text:
# Check container status
docker compose ps

# Check logs
docker compose logs -f

# Test health endpoint
curl http://localhost:8001/api/health

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create /opt/genslave/.env:

# Required: API secret (must match GenMaster's GENSLAVE_API_SECRET)
GENSLAVE_API_SECRET=your-secure-secret-here

# Optional: Failsafe timeout (seconds before failsafe triggers)
FAILSAFE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30

# Optional: Mock mode for testing without hardware
MOCK_HAT_MODE=false

# Optional: Apprise notification URLs (comma-separated)
APPRISE_URLS=tgram://bottoken/chatid

# Optional: Log level
LOG_LEVEL=INFO

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Variable Description Default GENSLAVE_API_SECRET Shared secret for API authentication Required FAILSAFE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Seconds without heartbeat before failsafe 30 MOCK_HAT_MODE Run without actual hardware false APPRISE_URLS Notification service URLs Empty LOG_LEVEL Logging verbosity INFO HOST Bind address 0.0.0.0 PORT Listen port 8001

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
The standard docker-compose.yaml:

services:
  genslave:
    image: rjsears/pizero_generator_control:genslave
    container_name: genslave
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env

    # Required for GPIO access
    privileged: true

    # Use host network for Tailscale
    network_mode: host

    volumes:
      - genslave_data:/opt/genslave/data
      - genslave_logs:/opt/genslave/logs
      - /var/run/dbus:/var/run/dbus:rw  # For WiFi management

    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python3", "-c", "import httpx; httpx.get('http://localhost:8001/api/health', timeout=5)"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

volumes:
  genslave_data:
  genslave_logs:

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: GenSlave exposes a REST API on port 8001. All endpoints require the X-API-Key header.

docs.title: Health & Status
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/health Health check with system status GET /api/failsafe/status Failsafe monitor status

docs.title: Relay Control
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/relay/state Get relay and arm status POST /api/relay/on Turn relay ON (requires armed) POST /api/relay/off Turn relay OFF (always allowed) POST /api/relay/arm Arm the automation POST /api/relay/disarm Disarm the automation

docs.title: Heartbeat
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /api/heartbeat Receive heartbeat from GenMaster

docs.title: System
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description GET /api/system System info (CPU, RAM, disk, network) POST /api/system/reboot Reboot the Pi POST /api/system/shutdown Shutdown the Pi

docs.title: Example Requests
docs.text:
# Get relay state
curl http://genslave:8001/api/relay/state \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET"

# Arm the relay
curl -X POST http://genslave:8001/api/relay/arm \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET"

# Turn relay ON
curl -X POST http://genslave:8001/api/relay/on \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET"

docs.title: Failsafe System
docs.text: The failsafe system is an independent safety mechanism that stops the generator if GenMaster communication is lost.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. GenMaster sends heartbeats every 10 seconds
  2. GenSlave tracks last heartbeat timestamp
  3. If no heartbeat received within timeout period:
  4. Relay is turned OFF (generator stops)
  5. Notification is sent (if configured)
  6. failsafe_triggered flag is set
  7. When heartbeat resumes:
  8. Failsafe state is cleared
  9. "Restored" notification is sent
  10. GenMaster can re-arm and restart if needed

docs.title: Dynamic Timeout
docs.text:
The failsafe timeout is calculated dynamically:

effective_timeout = heartbeat_interval × 3

GenMaster sends its heartbeat interval in each heartbeat, and GenSlave calculates 3 × interval as the timeout. This means:

  • Default heartbeat: 10 seconds → Timeout: 30 seconds
  • Custom heartbeat: 15 seconds → Timeout: 45 seconds

This allows the system to adapt if heartbeat timing changes.

docs.title: Failsafe Status
docs.text:
Check failsafe status:

curl http://genslave:8001/api/failsafe/status \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET"

Response: 

{
  "running": true,
  "last_heartbeat": 1714567890,
  "seconds_since_heartbeat": 5,
  "heartbeat_count": 1234,
  "failsafe_triggered": false,
  "timeout_seconds": 30,
  "heartbeat_interval": 10,
  "timeout_source": "genmaster"
}

docs.title: When Failsafe Triggers
docs.text:
• Relay OFF is forced (even if armed)
  • Notification sent via Apprise (if configured)
  • Log entry created
  • GenSlave continues accepting heartbeats - when restored, it will sync with GenMaster

docs.title: WiFi Configuration
docs.text: GenSlave includes WiFi management endpoints for configuration via GenMaster.

docs.title: Scan for Networks
docs.text:
curl http://genslave:8001/api/system/wifi/networks \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET"

docs.title: Add Known Network
docs.text:
Pre-configure a WiFi network for auto-connect:

curl -X POST http://genslave:8001/api/system/wifi/add \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "ssid": "MyNetwork",
    "password": "my-password",
    "auto_connect": true
  }'

docs.title: Connect to Network
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://genslave:8001/api/system/wifi/connect \
  -H "X-API-Key: YOUR_SECRET" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "ssid": "MyNetwork",
    "password": "my-password"
  }'

Note: WiFi management requires the D-Bus socket to be mounted (/var/run/dbus:/var/run/dbus:rw).

docs.title: Scheduled Reboot
docs.text: GenSlave supports scheduled maintenance reboots for long-term reliability.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Via API (proxied through GenMaster):

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/genslave/reboot-schedule \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "day": "sunday",
    "hour": 4,
    "minute": 0
  }'

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Field Description Options enabled Enable/disable scheduled reboots true/false day Day of week or daily monday-sunday or daily hour Hour (24-hour format) 0-23 minute Minute 0-59

docs.title: Safety Check
docs.text:
The scheduled reboot only executes if: - The relay is OFF (generator not running) - Schedule is enabled - Current time matches schedule

If the generator is running at the scheduled time, the reboot is skipped for that day.

docs.text:

  3. Ensure privileged: true in docker-compose.yaml

docs.title: Nginx Access Control and Real IP Configuration
docs.text: This document explains the nginx access control configuration for GenMaster, including how traffic from different sources (LAN, Cloudflare Tunnel, and Tailscale) is handled.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: GenMaster uses nginx as a reverse proxy with IP-based access control. The geo block in nginx.conf determines whether requests are treated as "internal" (full access) or "external" (blocked or limited access).

docs.title: Traffic Sources
docs.text: GenMaster can be accessed through three different paths:

docs.title: 1. Direct LAN Access (10.x.x.x, 192.168.x.x, etc.)
docs.text:
• Path: Client → Host port 443 → nginx container
  • What nginx sees: Real client IP (e.g., 10.200.40.2)
  • Why it works: Docker port publishing preserves source IP for external traffic

docs.title: 2. Cloudflare Tunnel Access
docs.text:
• Path: Client → Cloudflare Edge → cloudflared container → nginx container
  • What nginx sees without real_ip config: Docker network IP (172.x.x.x)
  • What nginx sees with real_ip config: Real client IP from X-Forwarded-For header
  • Why real_ip is needed: cloudflared container connects to nginx through Docker network

docs.title: 3. Tailscale Access
docs.text:
• Path: Client → Tailscale network → Host's Tailscale interface → Host port 443 → nginx container
  • What nginx sees: Docker gateway IP (172.x.x.x)
  • Why no headers: Tailscale runs in network_mode: host for GenMaster-GenSlave communication, so no proxy headers are added

docs.title: The geo Block (Access Control)
docs.text:
geo $access_level {
    default          "external";
    127.0.0.1/32     "internal";
    10.0.0.0/8       "internal";
    172.16.0.0/12    "internal";
    192.168.0.0/16   "internal";
    100.64.0.0/10    "internal";  # Tailscale CGNAT range
    # Custom ranges can be added via GenMaster UI
}

This block evaluates the client's IP (after real_ip processing) and sets $access_level to either "internal" or "external".

docs.title: The real_ip Configuration (Cloudflare)
docs.text:
# Trust Docker/internal networks as proxies
set_real_ip_from 172.16.0.0/12;
set_real_ip_from 10.0.0.0/8;
set_real_ip_from 192.168.0.0/16;
set_real_ip_from 100.64.0.0/10;
set_real_ip_from 127.0.0.1;

# Extract real client IP from header
real_ip_header X-Forwarded-For;
real_ip_recursive on;

When a request comes from a trusted proxy IP (Docker network), nginx looks at the X-Forwarded-For header to find the real client IP.

docs.title: Why Tailscale Uses network_mode: host
docs.text:
The Tailscale container uses network_mode: host for a critical reason:

GenMaster must be able to reach GenSlave over Tailscale when they are NOT on the same local network.

If Tailscale ran in a Docker bridge network: - The Tailscale interface (100.x.x.x) would only be accessible inside the Tailscale container - GenMaster (in its own Docker network) couldn't route to GenSlave's Tailscale IP - This would break GenMaster-GenSlave communication when they're on different networks

With network_mode: host: - The Tailscale interface is available on the host - GenMaster can reach GenSlave via Tailscale IP (100.x.x.x) from anywhere

docs.title: Trade-off
docs.text:
The trade-off is that Tailscale web traffic (via *.ts.net URLs) doesn't have real client IPs in nginx logs - you'll see 172.x.x.x instead. However:

  1. Tailscale traffic is already authenticated by Tailscale
  2. The 172.x.x.x IP falls within the "internal" range, so access is granted
  3. This is acceptable because only authenticated Tailscale users can reach the *.ts.net URL

docs.title: Summary Table
docs.text: Access Method Nginx Sees Access Level Notes LAN (10.x.x.x) Real IP internal Direct connection preserves IP Cloudflare (external IP) Real IP external real_ip extracts from X-Forwarded-For Cloudflare (trusted IP) Real IP internal If IP is in geo block Tailscale 172.x.x.x internal No headers, but Docker IP is "internal"

docs.title: Managing Access Control
docs.text:
IP ranges can be managed through the GenMaster UI: 1. Navigate to Settings → Access Control 2. Add or remove IP ranges as needed 3. Changes are written to nginx.conf and nginx is reloaded automatically

The access_control.py service only modifies the geo block - it preserves all other nginx configuration including the real_ip settings.

docs.title: Notifications Setup Guide
docs.text: This guide covers how to configure notifications for generator events using Apprise and system notification channels.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:

  • GenSlave Notifications
  • System Notification Events
  • Notification Channels
  • Testing Notifications
  • Troubleshooting

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The RPi Generator Control system supports notifications at two levels:

Component Purpose Notification Type GenMaster System events, generator status Channels + Groups GenSlave Failsafe alerts, local events Apprise URLs

docs.title: Notification Flow
docs.text:
Generator Event
      │
      ▼
┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│   GenMaster     │────►│ Notification    │────► Telegram, Slack,
│   Event         │     │ Channels        │      Email, etc.
└─────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘
      │
      │ Failsafe
      ▼
┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│   GenSlave      │────►│ Apprise         │────► Backup alerts
│   Failsafe      │     │ URLs            │      (independent)
└─────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘

docs.title: Apprise Integration
docs.text: Apprise is a notification library supporting 80+ services.

docs.title: Supported Services
docs.text: Service URL Format Telegram tgram://bottoken/chatid Slack slack://tokenA/tokenB/tokenC/channel Discord discord://webhook_id/webhook_token Pushover pover://user_key@api_token Email mailto://user:pass@gmail.com Twilio SMS twilio://account_sid:auth_token@from/to ntfy ntfy://topic Many more See Apprise Wiki

docs.text:
Telegram: 

tgram://123456789:AAHdqTcvCH1vGWJxfSeofSAs0K5PALDsaw/chatid

ntfy:

docs.title: GenMaster Notifications
docs.text: GenMaster uses a channel-based notification system with flexible grouping.

docs.title: Notification Channels
docs.text:
Create channels for each notification service:

Via Web UI: 1. Navigate to Settings > Notifications 2. Click Add Channel 3. Configure: - Name: Descriptive name (e.g., "My Telegram") - Type: Select service type - Configuration: Service-specific settings - Enabled: Toggle on/off

Via API: 

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/notifications/channels \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Main Telegram",
    "channel_type": "telegram",
    "config": {
      "bot_token": "123456789:AAHdqTcvCH1vGW...",
      "chat_id": "-1001234567890"
    },
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Notification Groups
docs.text:
Group channels together for different purposes:

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/notifications/groups \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Critical Alerts",
    "description": "High-priority notifications",
    "channel_ids": [1, 2, 3],
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Channel Types
docs.text: Type Config Fields telegram bot_token, chat_id slack webhook_url discord webhook_url email smtp_host, smtp_port, username, password, from_email, to_emails pushover user_key, api_token apprise urls (array of Apprise URLs) webhook url, headers, method

docs.title: GenSlave Notifications
docs.text: GenSlave uses Apprise URLs directly for failsafe notifications.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Via Environment Variable: 

# In .env file
APPRISE_URLS=tgram://token/chatid,slack://webhook

Via API (through GenMaster): 

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/genslave/notifications \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "apprise_urls": [
      "tgram://123456:ABC.../chatid",
      "slack://T00/B00/XXX"
    ]
  }'

docs.title: Notification Cooldown
docs.text:
Prevent notification spam with cooldown settings:

curl -X POST https://your-genmaster/api/genslave/notifications/settings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "failsafe_cooldown_minutes": 5,
    "restored_cooldown_minutes": 5
  }'

docs.text: Event When Triggered Failsafe Triggered Communication lost with GenMaster Heartbeat Restored Communication restored after failsafe

docs.title: System Notification Events
docs.text: GenMaster can send notifications for various system events.

docs.title: Available Events
docs.text: Event Description generator_started Generator has started generator_stopped Generator has stopped slave_connected GenSlave connection established slave_disconnected GenSlave connection lost override_enabled Manual override activated override_disabled Manual override deactivated exercise_started Exercise run started exercise_completed Exercise run completed max_runtime_reached Generator hit runtime limit lockout_activated Runtime lockout enabled lockout_cleared Runtime lockout cleared

docs.title: Configuring Event Notifications
docs.text:
Via Web UI: 1. Navigate to Settings > System Notifications 2. For each event type: - Toggle enabled/disabled - Select notification channels/groups - Configure message template (optional)

Via API: 

curl -X PUT https://your-genmaster/api/system-notifications/generator_started \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "channel_ids": [1, 2],
    "group_ids": [1],
    "title_template": "Generator Started",
    "body_template": "Generator started at {{start_time}} - Reason: {{reason}}"
  }'

docs.title: Template Variables
docs.text:
Templates support these variables:

Generator Events: - {{run_id}} - Run ID - {{start_time}} - Start timestamp - {{stop_time}} - Stop timestamp - {{runtime}} - Formatted runtime - {{reason}} - Start/stop reason - {{fuel_gallons}} - Fuel used - {{fuel_type}} - Fuel type

System Events: - {{timestamp}} - Event timestamp - {{status}} - Current status - {{details}} - Event details

docs.text:
1. Check channel is enabled:

  2. Check event is configured:

  3. Verify event type has channels assigned

1. Verify bot token:

  2. Verify chat ID:

  3. Message the bot first

  4. For groups, bot must be added to group

  5. Check bot permissions:

docs.text:
1. Check SMTP settings:
  2. Verify host and port

  3. Try port 465 (SSL) or 587 (TLS)

docs.text:

  2. Test manually with curl

docs.title: High Notification Volume
docs.text:
1. Enable cooldowns:
  2. Set appropriate cooldown periods

  3. Prevents notification spam

  4. Adjust event triggers:

docs.title: 1. Use Multiple Channels
docs.text: Configure backup notification channels: - Primary: Telegram/Slack - Backup: Email - Critical: SMS (Twilio)

docs.title: 2. Set Appropriate Cooldowns
docs.text: Prevent notification fatigue: - Failsafe notifications: 5-10 minute cooldown - Status updates: 1-5 minute cooldown

curl "https://your-genmaster/api/notifications/history?limit=50" \

docs.title: Hardware Configuration

docs.title: Key Architecture Decisions
docs.text:
1. GenMaster on Pi 5: Upgraded from Pi Zero 2W for better performance and Docker support
  2. PostgreSQL for GenMaster: Full-featured database with JSONB, async support via asyncpg
  3. SQLite for GenSlave: Zero-overhead file-based database to conserve RAM on Pi Zero 2W
  4. Native deployment for GenSlave: No Docker to save ~150MB RAM
  5. Docker Hub publishing: Multi-arch images (amd64/arm64) for GenMaster
